title: is_valid_pylock_path accepts file names with a trailing newline
spec:
This is the `packaging` library (Python 3, no dependencies; the code is in `src/packaging/`). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests --ignore=tests/property` (about a minute).

`packaging.pylock.is_valid_pylock_path` should only accept complete file names of the form `pylock.toml` or `pylock.<name>.toml`. A name with extra trailing characters is wrongly accepted.

```python
from pathlib import Path
from packaging.pylock import is_valid_pylock_path
print(is_valid_pylock_path(Path("pylock.spam.toml\n")))
```

EXPECTED: `False`
ACTUAL: `True`

The rule is that the whole file name must match the pattern, with nothing after the final `.toml` (not even a newline). Existing behaviour must stay: `pylock.toml` and `pylock.spam.toml` are valid; `pylock.json` and `pylock..toml` are invalid.
acceptance: pylock.toml and pylock.spam.toml still return True
pylock.json and pylock..toml still return False
